blind_target.title: Seeking subjective dominance in multidimensional space: An explanation of the asymmetric dominance effect.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
This article reports two very close replication studies of the decoy effect, targeting

Experiment 1 in Ariely and Wallsten (1995) and Experiment 1 in Connolly et al. (2013).
blind_target.outcome_quote:
We conducted a very close direct replication of Experiment 1 in Ariely and Wallsten

(1995). We failed to find support for the original results.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly give an overall verdict for this specific replication.

prior_decision.quote:
This article reports two very close replication studies of the decoy effect, targeting

Experiment 1 in Ariely and Wallsten (1995) and Experiment 1 in Connolly et al. (2013).
prior_decision.reason: In addition to replicating Connolly et al. (2013) in Study 2, the paper conducts a full direct replication of Experiment 1 from Ariely and Wallsten (1995) in Study 1 (reporting a failed replication outcome), making it an omitted replication target.

luna_triage.reason: The article explicitly identifies Study 1 as a replication of Experiment 1 in Ariely and Wallsten (1995), reports that this retest failed, and supplies the full reference and DOI. The only supplied shipped original is Connolly, Reb, and Kausel (2013), which is separately retested in Study 2 and is not the Ariely and Wallsten work.
luna_triage.omission_quote: We attempted to replicate Experiment 1 from Ariely and Wallsten (1995) (Study 1) and Experiment 1 from Connolly, Reb, and Kausel (2013) (Study 2). We failed to replicate the original results in Study 1.
luna_triage.identity_quote: Ariely, D., & Wallsten, T. S. (1995). Seeking subjective dominance in multidimensional space: An explanation of the asymmetric dominance effect. Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, 63(3), 223–232. https://doi.org/10.1006/obhd.1995.1075
